_comment: SYNTHETIC. Two fictional teams, part of the development set: originally written as held-out data, but a gpt-6-luna smoke test ran on them before the prompts and guard were final, so they are no longer blind. No real person wrote or is described by any note.

planted.summary: App store review delays held up releases
Flaky UI tests on CI waste time
Shared prototypes improved the design handoff (positive)
Need a quiet place for calls (below k)

notes.text: The app store review took four days and blocked our release.
Waiting on store approval again pushed the launch.
Release was ready on Monday but app review only cleared on Thursday.
Store review delays make our release dates meaningless.
We lost most of the week waiting for the app to be approved.
App review rejected the build over a screenshot, so we waited all over again.
The UI tests fail randomly and we rerun them three times.
Flaky end-to-end tests are wasting hours every day.
CI goes red for no reason, it is always the emulator tests.
I do not trust the test results any more because they flake.
Rerunning flaky UI tests is now part of my morning routine, like brushing my teeth with a cactus.
Unreliable automated tests slowed every merge.
Half my CI runs fail on tests that pass locally.
The clickable prototypes made the design handoff much clearer.
Working from a shared prototype saved a lot of back and forth with design.
Design handoff was much better this time thanks to the interactive mockups.
Seeing the prototype early answered most of my questions.
Prototypes before development started were really helpful.
We need a quiet room for customer calls.
Hard to take calls in the open office.
Since Joaquin went on leave, nobody knows how the push notification setup works.

planted.summary: On-call alerts are noisy and mostly not actionable

notes.text: Most alerts on call this week were false alarms.
The pager went off constantly for things that did not need action.
Alert noise makes it hard to spot the real problems.
Too many alerts fire for harmless spikes.
On call was exhausting because of noisy alerts that fixed themselves.
We should tune the alert thresholds, most pages were not actionable.
Alerts kept firing all night for nothing; on call felt like playing whack-a-mole in the dark.
Stakeholders sent the requirements after we had started building.
We got the final spec two days before the deadline.
Requirements keep arriving late, so we rework things.
Late changes from the business side meant redoing the pipeline twice.
Hard to plan when requirements show up mid-sprint.
The Friday knowledge-sharing sessions are really useful.
Learned a lot from the internal tech talks this sprint.
Loved the session where we walked through the ingestion jobs.
Knowledge sharing sessions helped me understand parts of the system I never touch.
Please keep the weekly learning sessions.
Dashboards take ages to load.
The reporting dashboards time out on large queries.
Our monitoring dashboards are painfully slow.
Not much to add.
